## Inito Review 2026: 4 Hormones, Cost & Who It's For

**Key takeaways**
- Inito measures four hormones — estrogen, LH, PdG, FSH — from one urine sample.
- PdG is the differentiator: it confirms ovulation happened, which LH-only strips cannot do.
- Running cost is the real consideration: strips are consumed daily across the fertile window.
- If you have regular cycles and only need ovulation timing, a cheaper LH strip is enough.

### What Inito is

Inito is a home fertility monitor: a phone-attached reader plus daily test strips that quantify four hormones rather than returning a binary positive or negative.

### Who this Inito review is for

This is for people choosing between four-hormone monitors and standard LH strips — most often those with irregular cycles, suspected [anovulation](https://example.com/blog/anovulation-symptoms), or a PCOS diagnosis, where LH-only testing is least reliable.

### How the four-hormone panel works

Estrogen rises as a follicle matures. LH surges 24–36 hours before ovulation. PdG rises after ovulation and confirms it occurred. FSH shows how hard the body is working to recruit a follicle. Measuring PdG alongside LH is what separates prediction from confirmation — a distinction covered in more depth in our guide to the [luteal phase](https://example.com/blog/luteal-phase-length).

A [2021 validation study in *Fertility and Sterility*](https://example.org/fertstert-pdg-validation) found urinary PdG thresholds agree closely with mid-luteal serum progesterone, and [ACOG's guidance on ovulatory dysfunction](https://example.org/acog-ovulatory-dysfunction) treats confirmed ovulation — not a predicted surge — as the clinically meaningful endpoint.

### What testing is actually like

Testing begins around cycle day 6 and continues daily through the fertile window and into the luteal phase. Each test is a mid-stream urine sample read by the device. Expect roughly 10–20 strips per cycle depending on cycle length and how long you test past ovulation.

If your cycles vary by more than a week month to month — common with [PCOS](https://example.com/blog/pcos-and-ovulation) — expect to test more days per cycle, because the fertile window is harder to bracket in advance. A [2023 cohort study in *Human Reproduction*](https://example.org/humrep-cycle-variability) put cycle-length variability above 9 days in roughly a fifth of people tracking at home.

### Inito vs Mira vs Clearblue

| | Inito | Mira | Clearblue Advanced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hormones measured | E3G, LH, PdG, FSH | E3G, LH, PdG, FSH | E3G, LH |
| Confirms ovulation | Yes (PdG) | Yes (PdG) | No |
| Quantified values | Yes | Yes | No — binary |
| Reader cost | Mid | Higher | Lowest |
| Per-cycle strip cost | Moderate | Higher | Lowest |
| Best for | Irregular cycles, PCOS | Irregular cycles | Regular cycles, timing only |

### Cost

Budget for the reader once and strips every cycle. The strips dominate total cost over a year, so per-cycle strip count matters more than the upfront device price when comparing options.

### What we'd flag

- **Cost compounds.** Several cycles of daily testing is a material recurring expense.
- **Data can become a source of anxiety.** Quantified daily hormone values are more information than some people want mid-cycle.
- **It is not diagnostic.** It confirms whether ovulation occurred; it does not diagnose why it didn't.
- **Regular cycles may not need it.** If you ovulate predictably and only need timing, an LH strip costs far less.

### Verdict

Worth it if you have irregular cycles or need ovulation *confirmed* rather than predicted. Skip it if your cycles are regular and you only need to time intercourse — the extra hormones won't change what you do.

### FAQ

**Does Inito confirm ovulation?** Yes — that is what the PdG measurement is for.

**Is Inito better than LH strips?** For irregular cycles, yes. For regular cycles where timing is the only question, the added cost is hard to justify.
